import pandas as pd

# List all source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_60/test_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_60/test_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_60/test_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_60/test_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_60/test_4.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_60/test_5.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_60/test_6.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_60/test_7.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_60/test_8.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_60/test_9.csv"
]

# Read all source tables into a list of DataFrames
dfs = []
for file_path in source_files:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0)
    # Ensure columns are exactly ['start', 'tendercare']
    df = df[['start', 'tendercare']]
    # Convert 'start' to string type (if not already)
    df['start'] = df['start'].astype(str)
    # Convert 'tendercare' to integer type (if not already)
    df['tendercare'] = df['tendercare'].astype(int)
    dfs.append(df)

# Since all source tables have the exact same schema as the target,
# we can union (concatenate) all source tables vertically.
target_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Optional: If the target examples have duplicates, we keep duplicates as is.
# The prompt does not specify removing duplicates, so we keep all rows.

# Write the resulting DataFrame to the target CSV file
target_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_60/target_multisource_cot.csv", index=False)
